title: August 2026 fresh-intake production - batch H1 (BMP Maritime Security: the family the bank had no card for)
note: ONE ACTION, ONE NEW CARD. AUG-0089 - 'what is bmp ms' - was asked on 27 August 2026 with five starred follow-up probes (AUG-0090 to AUG-0094) and asked again on 28 August (AUG-0196). Adjudication classified it GENUINE_NEW_QUESTION because every BMP card in the bank was edition-scoped to BMP5, so there was nothing to enrich. The five probes get headed blocks inside the one root card rather than five cards: they are the same ask examined from five sides, and splitting them would put five near-identical answers on one page. WHY THIS BATCH HAS A CORRECTION BESIDE IT. Producing the card established that BMP Maritime Security replaced BMP5, BMP West Africa and the Global Counter Piracy Guidance in 2025 and is now at its 2026 edition. Five live cards taught BMP5 as current. Those five are NOT this batch's work: they are corrected under CORR-BMP-MS-CURRENCY-20260831, which shares this baseline and names this manifest. The division is deliberate - this record authorises the card that did not exist, that record authorises the change to cards that did. EXAMINER ATTRIBUTION. No examiner name was added. Relationships stay at 958 and examiners at 7; the panel facts stay in the intake store. ACCESS LIMIT, STATED NOT HIDDEN. The BMP MS publication itself is served behind an HTTP 403 that was not defeated. The card therefore asserts NO chapter, page or phase structure, and says so to the candidate in its source-confidence line. Its sources are registered in docs/sources/MIW_SOURCE_REGISTRY.json as SRC-BMPMS-2026, SRC-BMPMS-2025 and SRC-MISTO-2025-11. FIRST ROUND WAS REJECTED. Independent review failed round 1 because the card taught the 31 March 2025 first edition as current. The currency record behind it had asked only 'does BMP MS supersede BMP5?' - a question that answers correctly and cannot reveal a later edition. The rule that produced is recorded under query_discipline in the source registry. MANIFEST REPAIR, 2026-08-31 (during H2). This record shipped with no authorisation_batch_key and with a produced_in_commit field the schema does not classify, so `python tools/oral/oral_manifest.py` was red on it. Nobody saw that, because H1 ran validate_corrections.py - which audits CORRECTION records - and never the manifest auditor itself. H2 ran it and found this. The key now resolves against a batches map added to the authorisation record; the unclassified field is folded into this note rather than deleted: action H1-001's post-edit digest was taken from commit 4ec0ba2, which is also the commit named in the companion correction's governing_commits. No card bytes changed.
